summary: Count to 100 by ones and by tens.
Count forward starting from any given number instead of starting at 1.
Write numerals 0 to 20 and use a numeral to show how many objects.
Link counting to quantity: one number per object, last number tells how many.
Count up to 20 objects in a line, array or circle (10 scattered) and count out sets.
Tell whether one group has more, fewer or the same number as another group.
Compare and order two written numbers from 0 to 20 (CCSS compares 1 to 10).
Show adding and taking away with objects, fingers, drawings, sounds, acting out or equations.
Solve addition and subtraction story problems within 10 using objects or drawings.
Split numbers up to 10 into two parts in more than one way and record each.
For a number 1 to 9, find what to add to make 10 and record it.
Add and subtract within 5 fluently.
Recognize and make patterns with colors, shapes, sizes and sounds, with adult support.
Build and break apart numbers 11 to 19 as ten ones and some more ones.
Describe things you can measure about an object, such as its length or weight.
Directly compare two objects to see which has more or less of an attribute.
Sort objects into categories, count each category (up to 10) and order categories by count.
Recognize pennies, nickels, dimes and quarters.
Count pennies up to 20.
Name shapes seen around you and describe where they are with position words.
Name shapes correctly no matter their size or which way they turn.
Tell whether real objects are flat (two-dimensional) or solid (three-dimensional) shapes.
Compare flat and solid shapes in everyday words: sides, corners and other features.
Build shapes from parts like sticks and clay, and draw shapes.
Put simple shapes together to make bigger shapes.
Solve addition and subtraction story problems within 20 with the unknown in any position.
Solve story problems that add three whole numbers with a total of 20 or less.
Use properties like changing order or grouping as strategies to add and subtract.
Treat subtraction as finding a missing addend.
Connect counting on and counting back to adding and subtracting.
Add and subtract within 20 with strategies like making ten; fluent within 10.
Know what the equal sign means, judge equations true or false, and tell expressions from equations.
Find the missing number in an addition or subtraction equation with three whole numbers.
Count, read and write numbers to 120 from any start; skip count by 2s, 5s and 10s.
Know that the two digits of a two-digit number mean tens and ones.
Compare and order two two-digit numbers using tens and ones, with >, = and <.
Add within 100 using models and place-value strategies, sometimes making a new ten.
Find 10 more or 10 less than a two-digit number in your head and explain.
Subtract multiples of 10 from multiples of 10 (10 to 90) with models and explain.
Order three objects by length and compare two lengths using a third object.
Measure length by laying copies of a shorter unit end to end with no gaps.
Tell and write time to the hour and half hour on analog and digital clocks.
Know coin values and trade pennies for dimes and dimes for a dollar like place value.
Organize and read data in up to three categories; answer total and how-many-more questions.
Tell defining features of shapes from non-defining ones and build or draw shapes.
Put flat or solid shapes together into a composite shape and make new shapes from it.
Split circles and rectangles into halves and fourths; more equal shares means smaller shares.
Make a pattern that follows a given rule using colors, shapes, sizes and sounds.
Solve one- and two-step addition and subtraction story problems within 100.
Add and subtract within 20 fluently and know all sums of two one-digit numbers by heart.
Look at a number pattern and find its rule: add 2, 3, 5 or 10.
Decide if a group of up to 20 is odd or even; write evens as a double.
Use repeated addition to total objects in arrays up to 5 by 5 and write the equation.
Know the digits of a three-digit number mean hundreds, tens and ones.
Count within 1,000 and skip count by 5s, 10s and 100s.
Read and write numbers to 1,000 as numerals, number names and expanded form.
Compare and order three-digit numbers by place value, using >, = and <.
Add and subtract within 100 fluently using place value and properties.
Add up to four two-digit numbers using place value and properties.
Add and subtract within 1,000 with models and place-value strategies, regrouping when needed.
Mentally add or subtract 10 or 100 to or from numbers 100 to 900.
Explain why addition and subtraction strategies work using place value and properties.
Measure length with the right tool: ruler, yardstick, meter stick or tape.
Measure an object with two different units and explain how the numbers relate to unit size.
Estimate lengths in inches, feet, centimeters and meters.
Measure to find how much longer one object is than another in standard units.
Solve length story problems in one unit using addition and subtraction within 100.
Show whole numbers, sums and differences within 100 on a number line.
Tell and write time to the nearest five minutes on analog and digital clocks, with a.m./p.m.
Solve money story problems with bills and coins using $ and cent signs.
Measure lengths to whole units and show the data on a line plot.
Draw picture and bar graphs for up to four categories and solve problems from them.
Draw shapes with given features; name triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons, hexagons and cubes.
Split a rectangle into rows and columns of equal squares and count them.
Split circles and rectangles into halves, thirds or fourths; equal shares can differ in shape.
Understand a product as the total in a number of equal groups.
Understand a quotient as the size of each share or the number of shares.
Solve multiplication and division story problems within 100 with groups, arrays and measures.
Find the missing number in a multiplication or division equation.
Use commutative, associative and distributive properties as strategies to multiply and divide.
Treat division as finding a missing factor.
Multiply and divide within 100 fluently; know the facts through the 10s by year end.
Solve two-step story problems with all four operations; check answers with estimation and rounding.
Find patterns in addition and multiplication tables and explain them with properties.
Read and write numbers to 10,000 in standard, word and expanded form.
Compare and order four-digit numbers by place value, using >, = and <.
Round whole numbers to the nearest 10 or 100.
Add and subtract within 1,000 fluently using place-value strategies and algorithms.
Multiply one-digit numbers by multiples of 10 from 10 to 90.
Understand unit fractions 1/b and fractions a/b as counts of unit parts.
Place fractions on a number line by splitting 0 to 1 into equal parts.
Find simple equivalent fractions, write wholes as fractions, and compare same-numerator or same-denominator fractions.
Tell time to the minute and solve elapsed-time problems in minutes.
Measure and estimate liquid volume and mass in liters, grams and kilograms; solve one-step problems.
Draw scaled picture and bar graphs and solve how-many-more and how-many-less problems.
Measure lengths to the nearest half or quarter inch and show data on a line plot.
Understand area as covering a flat figure with unit squares.
Find area by counting unit squares in metric, customary or made-up units.
Link area to multiplying and adding, including tiling, the distributive property and rectilinear shapes.
Solve perimeter problems, find a missing side, and compare rectangles by area and perimeter.
See that shape categories share features; know rhombuses, rectangles and squares are quadrilaterals.
Split shapes into parts of equal area and name each part as a unit fraction.
Read a multiplication equation as a times-as-many comparison.
Multiply or divide to solve comparison story problems; tell them apart from additive comparisons.
Solve multi-step whole-number story problems, interpreting remainders and checking with estimation.
Find factor pairs for numbers to 100, recognize multiples, and tell prime from composite.
Make a number pattern from a rule and notice features the rule does not state.
Know each place is worth ten times the place to its right.
Read, write, compare and order multi-digit whole numbers in several forms.
Round multi-digit whole numbers to any place.
Add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers fluently with the standard algorithm.
Multiply up to four digits by one digit and two-digit by two-digit numbers with models.
Divide up to four-digit numbers by one-digit numbers, with remainders, using models and partial quotients.
Explain equivalent fractions with models and use the idea to make equivalent fractions.
Compare fractions with different numerators and denominators using common parts or benchmarks.
Add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers with like denominators and decompose fractions.
Multiply a fraction by a whole number and solve related story problems.
Rewrite tenths as hundredths and add fractions with denominators 10 and 100.
Write tenths and hundredths fractions as decimals and place them on a number line.
Compare two decimals to hundredths by reasoning about size, with >, = and <.
Know relative sizes of units and convert larger units to smaller ones in a table.
Solve story problems on distance, time, volume, mass and money, including fractions and decimals.
Use area and perimeter formulas for rectangles, including finding a missing side.
Make line plots with half, quarter and eighth units and solve problems from them.
Understand angles as two rays from one point, measured in degrees of a circle.
Measure angles to whole degrees with a protractor and sketch given angles.
Add angle measures and find unknown angles in diagrams.
Draw and find points, lines, segments, rays, angle types, and parallel or perpendicular lines.
Sort flat figures by parallel or perpendicular lines and angle types; identify right triangles.
Find and draw lines of symmetry in flat figures.
Evaluate number expressions that use parentheses or brackets.
Write expressions for described calculations and read expressions without computing them.
Make two number patterns from two rules, relate their terms and graph the pairs.
Know a digit is worth ten times the place to its right and a tenth of the left.
Explain how multiplying or dividing by powers of 10 changes a number; use exponents for them.
Read, write and compare decimals to thousandths, including expanded form.
Round multi-digit numbers, including decimals, to any place.
Multiply multi-digit whole numbers fluently with the standard algorithm.
Divide up to four-digit numbers by two-digit numbers using models and partial quotients.
Add, subtract, multiply and divide decimals to hundredths using models and strategies.
Add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators by finding equivalent fractions.
Solve fraction addition and subtraction story problems and check answers with benchmark fractions.
See a fraction as division of numerator by denominator and solve related story problems.
Multiply a fraction or whole number by a fraction, including areas with fractional sides.
See multiplication as scaling and predict whether a product grows or shrinks.
Solve real-world problems multiplying fractions and mixed numbers.
Divide unit fractions by whole numbers and whole numbers by unit fractions, including story problems.
Convert units within the customary or metric system and use them in multi-step problems.
Make line plots with fractional measurements and solve problems using fraction operations.
Understand volume as packing a solid with unit cubes.
Find volume by counting unit cubes in cubic cm, in, ft or made-up units.
Find volumes of rectangular prisms with formulas and add volumes of two joined prisms.
Understand the coordinate plane: axes, origin and ordered pairs.
Graph points in the first quadrant to solve problems and interpret the coordinates.
Know that features of a shape category belong to all its subcategories.
Classify flat figures in a hierarchy by their properties.

state_code: # - Policy 2520.2B (W. Va. 126CSR44BB), West Virginia College- and Career-Readiness Standards for Mathematics: filed Aug 29, 2023, effective July 1, 2024 (amends the 2016 version).
#   Word: https://apps.sos.wv.gov/adlaw/csr/readfile.aspx?DocId=56641&Format=WORD (text used here; the PDF at &Format=PDF is an image scan)
#   Reached via the WVBE policy directory https://wveis.k12.wv.us/wvboe/policies/ (policy.php?p=2520.2B), which still links this filing on 2026-10-01.
# - Currency for 2026-27: no later amendment found; WVDE grade-level standards PDFs were re-saved 2026-07-23 and match the policy text
#   The older wvde.us/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/... links (incl. the earlier wv5.pdf download) now return a not-found page.
# - No official WV-to-CCSS alignment or 2016-to-2024 crosswalk was found on wvde.us; every ccss mapping here is my own reading of the text.
# - M.<grade>.<n>: M = mathematics, grade K or 1-5, standards numbered continuously within each grade (e.g. M.3.18).
# - Some standards carry lettered/bulleted sub-parts (e.g. M.3.24, M.4.14, M.5.17); these restate CCSS sub-parts and are folded into the standard.
# - Mathematical Habits of Mind (MHM1-MHM8, = CCSS practices) are skipped.
# - Typo in the WVDE grade 3 PDF: M.3.15 is printed as a second "M.3.13"; the policy text has M.3.15.
# DOMAINS / CLUSTERS (same names as CCSS; WV lists number ranges per cluster)
# - K: Counting and Cardinality (know number names; count to tell the number; compare numbers), Operations and Algebraic Thinking
#   (addition/subtraction meaning; Recognize patterns), Number and Operations in Base Ten (11-19), Measurement and Data (measurable attributes;
#   classify and count; Work with money), Geometry (identify and describe shapes; analyze, compare, create, compose shapes).
# - 1: OA (represent/solve; properties; add and subtract within 20; equations), NBT (extend counting; place value; add/subtract), MD (length;
#   Work with time and money; data), G (reason with shapes).
# - 2: OA (represent/solve; add/subtract and arithmetic patterns; equal groups), NBT (place value; add/subtract), MD (measure/estimate length;
#   relate add/subtract to length; Work with time and money; data), G.
# - 3: OA, NBT, NF (fractions as numbers), MD (time/volume/mass; data; area; perimeter), G. 4: OA, NBT, NF, MD, G. 5: OA, NBT, NF, MD, G (CCSS clusters).
# - None: every CCSS K-5 standard maps to a WV standard (2.MD.C.8 and 4.NBT.A.2 also absorb earlier WV coin and four-digit work).
# - New: patterns in K (M.K.13), grade 1 (M.1.23, follow a rule) and grade 2 (M.2.3, find an add-2/3/5/10 rule).
# - Moved earlier: coins in K (identify all four coins, count pennies to 20) and grade 1 (coin values, pennies/dimes as place value), from 2.MD.C.8;
#   skip counting by 2s, 5s, 10s to 120 in grade 1 (CCSS 2.NBT.A.2); reading, writing, comparing and ordering numbers to 10,000 in grade 3 (CCSS 4.NBT.A.2).
# - Small extensions kept as same: "order" added to comparisons (M.1.11, M.2.9), facts through 10s in grade 3, mixed numbers between wholes (M.4.14).
# - Edited: M.K.7 compares/orders numbers 0-20 (CCSS 1-10); M.1.7 adds expression vs equation.
# - M.2.3 (find a pattern rule) marked new; it is near 3.OA.D.9 / 4.OA.C.5 but runs the other way (rule from pattern) and is much simpler.
# - M.K.18, M.K.19, M.1.18 mapped to 2.MD.C.8 as moved; CCSS has no coin standard before grade 2. M.1.18 also echoes 1.NBT.B.2 (ten ones = one ten).
# - M.1.9 combines 1.NBT.A.1 with grade-2 skip counting (2.NBT.A.2); marked edited.
# - M.3.10 and M.3.11 (four-digit numbers) mapped to 4.NBT.A.2 as moved: CCSS place value stops at 1,000 in grade 2 and has no grade-3 read/write/compare standard.
# - kind is judged on content: same = CCSS content with only rewording, examples or small range tweaks.
